findings.summary: Parameters containing expressions and same-name body vars share a symbol despite distinct runtime environments.
findings.expected: Parameter initializer closures reference the parameter binding; a same-name body var is a separate binding with an initial value transfer. Body writes must not rewrite the parameter binding identity.
findings.observed: identity(param) === identity(bodyVar), with both declarations present on the same TypeScript symbol. Confirmed in .mts and .mjs parse-only proofs.
findings.cause: The correction only looks outward when every runtime declaration is inside the body. A merged parameter + var symbol fails that predicate, and no distinct body/parameter key is allocated.
findings.impact: The capability fixed points and stable-initializer/reference analyses consume the conflated key. This violates the requested precision and cannot establish absence of parameter/body contamination. No native exploit or additional adversarial capability fixture was generated.
findings.requiredCorrection: Model separate parameter and body var bindings for parameter lists containing expressions, preserving explicit initial-value transfer and keeping the legitimately shared simple-parameter case.

findings.summary: A body reference resolves to a parameter instead of the same-name body function.
findings.expected: The initializer closure token refers to the parameter; return token in the body refers to the hoisted body function.
findings.observed: identity(returnToken) === identity(parameterToken); identity(returnToken) !== identity(bodyFunctionToken). Confirmed in .mts and .mjs parse-only proofs.
findings.cause: The helper accepts checker.getSymbolAtLocation for body references. The parameter-only ancestry correction never revisits body references, so the TypeScript binder choice survives unchanged.
findings.impact: Body reads and the actual body declaration disagree on symbol identity. Classification can attach the wrong origin to body references; precise static binding is not established. No offensive payload or native evaluation was run.
findings.requiredCorrection: Resolve references in the body against its actual runtime body environment, while preserving parameter/outer resolution for initializer closures.
